claims.text: Powder-pack boriding produces a surface boride layer on a metallic component.
Increasing powder-pack boriding duration and temperature will increase the boride-layer thickness.
Extended high-temperature powder-pack boriding will increase the density of the boride surface layer.
Extended high-temperature powder-pack boriding will make the boride surface layer more continuous.
A thicker, denser, and more continuous boride layer acts as a physical barrier against molten aluminum.
A denser and thicker boride layer reduces direct contact between molten aluminum and the underlying metal substrate.
A denser and thicker boride layer reduces interdiffusion between molten aluminum and the substrate.
Reduced aluminum penetration minimizes corrosive attack on the underlying substrate.
Extended-borided components will have lower aluminum penetration than conventionally borided components.
Extended-borided components will have lower corrosion depths than conventionally borided components.
Extended-borided components will have less weight loss during molten-aluminum exposure than conventionally borided components.
The protective effect will persist under hot-dip aluminum-plating conditions as long as the boride phase remains structurally intact.
Boride-layer phase transformation or embrittlement at plating temperatures can eliminate or reduce the protective effect.
Increasing boride-layer thickness beyond a critical value may diminish the corrosion-resistance benefit.
